items.claim: The seven-item enumeration completing the six/seven formula (6:16-19) is byte-confirmed and correctly bounded, and the span's one K/Q note is properly disclosed as bearing on the noun's number/state rather than the count.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms שֶׁשׁ הֵ֭נָּה...וְ֝שֶׁ֗בַע (oshb:Prov.6.16) and the ketiv/qere pair תועבות תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת (oshb:Prov.6.16) both at BYTE tier; WEB 6:17-19 names exactly seven items (arrogant eyes, lying tongue, bloodshedding hands, a scheming heart, evil-swift feet, a false witness, a discord-sower) -- sweep-countable at 7, matching the row's enumeration; pmarks_Prov.json confirms petuchah (PE) at both Prov.6.15 and Prov.6.19, correctly labeled tier-3/single-witness; the kq inventory lists exactly one K/Q note in this span (Prov.6.16), and it is disclosed.

items.claim: The span (6:20-23) omits disclosure of the paseq mark at 6:22, a span-relevant mark the campaign's mark-disclosure symmetry rule requires unconditionally.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json's paseq inventory carries an entry at Prov.6.22, which sits inside this row's own Prov.6.20-Prov.6.23 span, but the row's boundary_evidence_refs, observed_substrate_signals, and device_notes disclose only the adjoining petuchahs at 6:19 and 6:26 -- the paseq at 6:22 is never named anywhere in the row, breaking the same unconditional span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry that this row's own cluster-mates observe correctly (P04-001 discloses the paseq at 7:12; P04-004 discloses the paseq at 8:29 and 8:30). The vocative-restart and metaphor-closure argument for the 6:20-23 boundary is otherwise sound: נְצֹ֣ר בְּ֭נִי מִצְוַ֣ת אָבִ֑יךָ (oshb:Prov.6.20) and נֵ֣ר מִ֭צְוָה וְת֣וֹרָה א֑וֹר (oshb:Prov.6.23) both collate at BYTE tier.

items.claim: The governing purpose-infinitive reading spanning 6:24-29 is byte-confirmed at both edges, and the span's one interior mark (petuchah at 6:26) is correctly disclosed as non-driving.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת רָ֑ע (oshb:Prov.6.24) and כֵּ֗ן הַ֭בָּא אֶל אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Prov.6.29) both at BYTE tier; pmarks_Prov.json confirms the petuchah (PE) at Prov.6.26 exists and the row correctly discloses it as tier-3/single-witness and non-operative rather than the seam driver; the pmarks paseq and kq inventories carry no entries anywhere inside Prov.6.24-Prov.6.29, so there is no symmetry gap in this span.

items.claim: The thief-versus-adulterer a fortiori span (6:30-35) is byte-confirmed at its opener and correctly bounded at the chapter-closing petuchah, with no undisclosed marks inside it.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms לֹא יָב֣וּזוּ לַ֭גַּנָּב (oshb:Prov.6.30) at BYTE tier, matching the row's subject-shift claim; the sevenfold-restitution reading of 6:31 (sheva'tayim) and the wounds/dishonor/vengeance/ransom content of 6:32-35 all check against the WEB text; pmarks_Prov.json confirms the petuchah (PE) at Prov.6.35, correctly disclosed tier-3/single-witness; the paseq and kq inventories carry no entries inside Prov.6.30-Prov.6.35.

items.claim: The row reads the purpose-infinitive opener at 7:5 as unit-internal continuity, but the byte-identical opening word recurs (sweep-confirmed) at only one other place in the book, 6:24, which this cluster's own two rows earlier treat as what starts a fresh unit, and this row's rejected_alternative never tests the analogous split at 7:4/7:5.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel "לשמרך" returns exactly 2 book-wide verse hits, Prov.6.24 and Prov.7.5 (skeleton tier) -- the ONLY two occurrences of this "to-guard-you" infinitive opener in Proverbs; collate.py confirms the shared opening word itself, לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ (oshb:Prov.6.24) and לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ (oshb:Prov.7.5), both at BYTE tier against their own verses (the two openers are byte-identical in this first word only -- the following noun phrase differs, לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה מִ֝נָּכְרִיָּ֗ה אֲמָרֶ֥יהָ הֶחֱלִֽיקָה at 7:5 vs the construct phrase at 6:24, so this challenge rests on the opener, not a longer shared phrase). P03-009's own rejected_alternative treats the 6:24 opener as what STARTS a fresh unit ("6:24 opens an infinitive-of-purpose clause naming a new addressee-threat... that the lamp/light metaphor of 6:20-23 has not yet introduced"), while this row treats the same opener at 7:5 as continuous with the preceding general address בְּ֭נִי (oshb:Prov.7.1) through 7:4, resting its "no fresh unit" reading only on the causal כִּ֭י of oshb:Prov.7.6. The row's rejected_alternative considers only a split at 7:5/7:6 ("isolating Prov.7.1-7.5 from the window scene"); it never engages the 7:4/7:5 split that this cluster's own 6:24 precedent, on the sweep-confirmed shared opener, would predict.

items.claim: The plural-address closing bracket (7:24-27) is byte-confirmed and echoes 7:1 through a genuine shared root, not an English-only parallel, with both edge petuchahs correctly disclosed.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ לִ֑י (oshb:Prov.7.24) at BYTE tier; the echo claim against 7:1 is grounded in Hebrew, not translation texture: the vocative root is shared (בְּ֭נִי at 7:1 / the plural of the same root at 7:24), and the "my words"/"the words of my mouth" figures share the root amar (אֲמָרָ֑י at 7:1 vs the construct plural of the same root at 7:24); pmarks_Prov.json confirms petuchah (PE) at both Prov.7.23 and Prov.7.27, correctly disclosed; the paseq and kq inventories carry no entries inside Prov.7.24-Prov.7.27.

items.claim: The span (8:1-21) omits disclosure of three span-relevant marks (paseq at 8:13, paseq at 8:21, and a ketiv/qere note at 8:17) and, at both of its internal candidate seams, states parashah silence itself as the ground for merging rather than splitting -- the inverse of the campaign's own standing rule that parashah absence is never a boundary argument in either direction.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json lists paseq at Prov.8.13 and Prov.8.21 and a ketiv/qere note at Prov.8.17 (kq count 1) -- all three fall inside this row's Prov.8.1-Prov.8.21 span and none is named anywhere in the row (the petuchah at 8:21 IS disclosed, but the co-located paseq at that same verse is not). The 8:17 K/Q is a live inline-ketiv case: unpointed ketiv אהביה ("who love her", 3fs) sits before the pointed qere אֹהֲבַ֣י ("who love me", 1cs) inside the very first-person self-commendation (8:12-21) this row argues runs unbroken -- exactly the inline-ketiv class TOOLKIT.md flags for disclosure before any claim about that span's voice is made. Separately, at both internal seams the row's stated warrant is parashah silence itself: for 8:3/8:4, "Nothing in the parashah layer marks a seam between the narrator's setup (8.1-3) and the call proper (8.4ff), so the two stay in one span"; for 8:11/8:12, "nothing in the parashah layer marks a seam at that point, so the call and the gift-commendation remain grouped." TOOLKIT.md's own rule -- "Absence is NEVER counterevidence"; parashah is tier-3, "never a boundary driver" -- forecloses using PE/SAMEKH silence as the stated ground for a merge decision, and this row does so at two separate joints.
tier_citations: tier-3 (PE/SAMEKH absence) -- misapplied as a merge warrant x2
